vercel-labs/agent-browser

Browser automation CLI for AI agents

Language: Rust

Stars: 48,443

Forks: 3,299

Stars today: 916 stars today

README

# agent-browser

Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell.

<p>
  <a href="https://vercel.com/labs#labs-products"><img alt="Vercel Labs Product" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/LABS-PRODUCT-0a0a0a.svg?style=for-the-badge&logo=Vercel&labelColor=000000" height="28"></a>
  <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/agent-browser"><img alt="npm version: agent-browser" src="https://img.shields.io/npm/v/agent-browser.svg?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=000000" height="28"></a>
  <a href="https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser/blob/main/LICENSE"><img alt="License: Apache-2.0" src="https://img.shields.io/github/license/vercel-labs/agent-browser.svg?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=000000" height="28"></a>
  <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/agent-browser"><img alt="npm downloads per month: agent-browser" src="https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/agent-browser.svg?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=000000&label=npm%20downloads" height="28"></a>
  <a href="https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-browser"><img alt="skills.sh" src="https://skills.sh/b/vercel-labs/agent-browser?style=for-the-badge" height="28"></a>
</p>

agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. `snapshot` returns the page as compact text with a ref such as `@e1` for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one short shell call.

## Install

```bash
npm install -g agent-browser
agent-browser install           # download Chrome for Testing (first time only)
```

- **Homebrew:** `brew install agent-browser`, then `agent-browser install`.
- **Linux:** `agent-browser install --with-deps` also installs the browser's system libraries.
- **No install:** `npx agent-browser open example.com`.

Project installs, building from source, `upgrade`, and `doctor` are covered in [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation).

## Quick start

```bash
agent-browser open example.com
agent-browser snapshot -i       # interactive elements, each with a ref
agent-browser click @e1         # act on a ref from that snapshot
agent-browser get url           # check the result
agent-browser close
```

The snapshot for `example.com`:

```
- link "Learn more" [ref=e1]
```

- Refs describe the page at the time of the snapshot. After navigation or a DOM change, take a new snapshot before using refs again.
- CSS selectors, text, XPath, and semantic locators also work, for example `agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit"`. See [Selectors](https://agent-browser.dev/selectors).
- A click fails, instead of reporting success, when the target is hidden, disabled, outside the viewport, or covered by another element such as a consent banner. Dismiss the covering element, take a new snapshot, and retry.

The full walkthrough is in the [quick start](https://agent-browser.dev/quick-start).

## How it works

The CLI sends each command to a background daemon that starts on the first command and controls the browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Each `--session` gets its own daemon and browser. By default, the daemon closes a headless browser and exits after one hour without commands, saving state first when [session persistence](https://agent-browser.dev/sessions) is configured.

Chrome for Testing is the default browser. You can also attach to a running Chrome with `--cdp` or `--auto-connect` ([CDP mode](https://agent-browser.dev/cdp-mode)), select the [Lightpanda](https://agent-browser.dev/engines/lightpanda) or [Obscura](https://agent-browser.dev/engines/obscura) engine with `--engine`, drive Mobile Safari in the [iOS Simulator](https://agent-browser.dev/ios), or use a cloud browser provider such as [Browserbase](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browserbase), [Browserless](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browserless), [Browser Use](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browser-use), [Kernel](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/kernel), or [AgentCore](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/agentcore).

## For AI agents

The CLI ships skills that match its version:

```bash
agent-browser skills get core                 # the core loop, refs, waiting, and common workflows
agent-browser skills get core --ref commands  # one reference, such as the full command list
agent-browser skills get core --full          # adds the full command reference and templates
agent-browser skills list                     # specialized skills: electron, slack, dogfood, and more
```

Install the discovery skill into an agent harness from [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-browser):

```bash
npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-browser
```

The installed skill is a thin stub that tells the agent to load `agent-browser skills get core`, so its instructions always match the installed CLI. Or add this to your `AGENTS.md`:

```markdown
Use `agent-browser` for browser automation. Before the first use, run
`agent-browser skills get core` and follow it.
```

For MCP clients, `agent-browser mcp` starts an MCP server over stdio. See [MCP server](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#mcp-server).

## Commands

Run `agent-browser --help` for the full list, or `agent-browser <command> --help` for one command.

| Group | Commands | Docs |
|---|---|---|
| Navigate and read | `open`, `back`, `forward`, `reload`, `read`, `snapshot`, `get`, `is` | [Core](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#core), [Snapshots](https://agent-browser.dev/snapshots) |
| Interact | `click`, `dblclick`, `fill`, `type`, `press`, `keyboard`, `hover`, `focus`, `select`, `check`, `uncheck`, `scroll`, `drag`, `upload`, `mouse`, `find` | [Core](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#core), [Find elements](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#find-elements) |
| Wait | `wait` | [Wait](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#wait) |
| Capture | `screenshot`, `pdf`, `record`, `download`, `diff` | [Recording](https://agent-browser.dev/recording), [Diffing](https://agent-browser.dev/diffing), [Files](https://agent-browser.dev/files) |
| Page and network state | `cookies`, `storage`, `network`, `set`, `clipboard`, `eval`, `pushstate` | [Network](https://agent-browser.dev/network), [Settings](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#settings) |
| Tabs, frames, and dialogs | `tab`, `frame`, `dialog` | [Tabs and frames](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#tabs-frames) |
| Debug and performance | `console`, `errors`, `highlight`, `inspect`, `trace`, `profiler`, `vitals`, `react`, `a11y` | [Debugging](https://agent-browser.dev/debugging), [Profiler](https://agent-browser.dev/profiler), [React](https://agent-browser.dev/react) |
| Sessions and auth | `session`, `state`, `auth`, `profiles`, `confirm`, `deny` | [Sessions](https://agent-browser.dev/sessions), [Security](https://agent-browser.dev/security) |
| Agents and integrations | `skills`, `mcp`, `webmcp`, `flow`, `chat`, `batch`, `plugin` | [Skills](https://agent-browser.dev/skills), [WebMCP](https://agent-browser.dev/webmcp), [Plugins](https://agent-browser.dev/plugins) |
| Observe | `stream`, `dashboard` | [Streaming](https://agent-browser.dev/streaming), [Dashboard](https://agent-browser.dev/dashboard) |
| Setup | `install`, `upgrade`, `doctor`, `connect`, `close` | [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation) |

Flags, environment variables, and `agent-browser.json` are documented in [Configuration](https://agent-browser.dev/configuration).

## Platforms

Native binaries ship for macOS (ARM64, x64), Linux (ARM64, x64, glibc and musl), and Windows (x64). The npm package picks the right binary for the host.

## Development

Building from source requires Node.js 24 or later, pnpm 11 or later, and Rust:

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm build:source               # builds the dashboard and the native CLI
pnpm link --global
agent-browser install
```

Run the Rust checks from `cli/`:

```bash
cargo fmt -- --check
cargo clippy
cargo test
cargo test e2e -- --ignored --test-threads=1   # launches real headless Chrome
```

[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) lists the files to update with each change, the docs checks, and the release process.

## Documentation

- [agent-browser.dev](https://agent-browser.dev): introduction, guides, and reference
- [Commands](https://agent-browser.dev/commands) and [Configuration](https://agent-browser.dev/configuration)
- [Security](https://agent-browser.dev/security): the auth vault, domain allowlists, action policies, and content boundaries
- [Next.js and Vercel](https://agent-browser.dev/next) and [eve](https://agent-browser.dev/eve): running agent-browser in Vercel Sandbox and eve agents
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)

## **See through walls with WiFi** ##

**Turn ordinary WiFi into a spatial intelligence / sensing system.** Detect people, measure breathing and heart rate, track movement, and monitor rooms — through walls, in the dark, with no cameras or wearables. Just physics.

Works natively with the four major smart-home ecosystems: **[Home Assistant](docs/integrations/home-assistant.md)** via the HA-DISCO MQTT publisher, **[Apple Home & HomePod](docs/user-guide-apple-homepod.md)** as a discoverable HAP-1.1 bridge, **[Google Home](docs/integrations/home-assistant.md)** + **[Amazon Alexa](docs/integrations/home-assistant.md)** via the same HA bridge or a [Matter](docs/adr/ADR-122-bfld-ruview-ha-matter-exposure.md) endpoint. Siri, Google Assistant, and Alexa can voice presence and vitals by room with zero custom skills.

[![Works with Home Assistant](https://img.shields.io/badge/Works%20with-Home%20Assistant-blue?logo=home-assistant&logoColor=white&labelColor=41BDF5)](docs/integrations/home-assistant.md) [![Works with Matter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Works%20with-Matter-blue?labelColor=4285F4)](docs/adr/ADR-122-bfld-ruview-ha-matter-exposure.md) [![Works with Apple Home](https://img.shields.io/badge/Works%20with-Apple%20Home-black?logo=apple)](docs/user-guide-apple-homepod.md) [![Works with Google Home](https://img.shields.io/badge/Works%20with-Google%20Home-blue?logo=googlehome)](docs/integrations/home-assistant.md) [![Works with Alexa](https://img.shields.io/badge/Works%20with-Alexa-blue?logo=amazon&logoColor=white&labelColor=00CAFF)](docs/integrations/home-assistant.md)

> Drop into any **Home Assistant** install with one `--mqtt` flag. Or pair into **Apple Home / Google Home / Alexa / SmartThings** as a Matter Bridge. Ships 21 entities per node (11 raw signals + 10 inferred semantic states: someone-sleeping, possible-distress, room-active, elderly-inactivity-anomaly, meeting-in-progress, bathroom-occupied, fall-risk-elevated, bed-exit, no-movement, multi-room-transition) plus 3 starter HA Blueprints. See [`docs/integrations/home-assistant.md`](docs/integrations/home-assistant.md) · [ADR-115](docs/adr/ADR-115-home-assistant-integration.md).

### π RuView is a WiFi sensing platform that turns radio signals into spatial intelligence.

Every WiFi router already fills your space with radio waves. When people move, breathe, or even sit still, they disturb those waves in measurable ways. RuView captures these disturbances using Channel State Information (CSI) from low-cost ESP32 sensors and turns them into actionable data: who's there, what they're doing, and whether they're okay.

[![Explore RuView sensing, models and automation](assets/readme/header-features-spatial-v4.svg)](docs/user-guide.md)

**What it senses:**
- **Presence and occupancy** — detect people through walls, count them, track entries and exits
- **Vital signs** — breathing rate and heart rate, contactless, while sleeping or sitting
- **Activity recognition** — walking, sitting, gestures, falls — from temporal CSI patterns
- **Environment mapping** — RF fingerprinting identifies rooms, detects moved furniture, spots new objects
- **Sleep quality** — overnight monitoring with sleep stage classification and apnea screening

**Also included:**

- **Camera-free pose** — estimate 17 body keypoints from WiFi CSI
- **Built-in model workflow** — record CSI, train models, load RVF files, and switch LoRA profiles
- **Local automation** — HOMECORE provides state, history, automations, signed Wasm plugins, voice hooks, and HomeKit support
- **Unified RF world model** — combine WiFi CSI, radar, UWB, and cellular sensing in one privacy-bounded scene model; accuracy is still synthetic until real-data validation
- **Governed evidence** — attach privacy policy, uncertainty, provenance, and witness records to sensing events
- **RuView MetaHarness** — use an AI operator to onboard, calibrate, train, verify, and check sensing claims

<details>
<summary><strong>RuView MetaHarness</strong> — guided operation for humans and AI agents</summary>

The RuView-specific metaharness we created is published as [`@ruvnet/ruview`](harness/ruview/README.md). It provides:
- source-cited guidance;
- device access for CSI nodes, radar and LiDAR;
- firmware flashing with boot evidence;
- one MCP server, usable over stdio or HTTP for ChatGPT, with a live console widget;
- a Claude Code mod;
- guarded Claude Code/Codex agents;
- deterministic verification;
- an honesty check for accuracy claims.

Companion packages: [`homecore`](harness/homecore/README.md) (Homecore developer metaharness) and [`@ruvnet/ruview-kernel`](harness/ruview-kernel/README.md) (the vitals pipeline as WASM).

```bash
# Check the local setup and get source-cited guidance
npx @ruvnet/ruview@0.9.1 doctor
npx @ruvnet/ruview@0.9.1 guidance --topic sensing --query "model loading"

# Hardware: what is plugged in, live CSI from your nodes, a 60 GHz radar kit
npx @ruvnet/ruview@0.9.1 devices
npx @ruvnet/ruview@0.9.1 esp32 --watch                       # ESP32 + Realtek RAC1 nodes, live view
npx @ruvnet/ruview@0.9.1 esp32 --seconds 45 --analyze        # live CSI through the vitals kernel
npx @ruvnet/ruview@0.9.1 mmwave --source esphome --host <kit-ip>

# Agents: MCP over stdio, or over HTTP for ChatGPT (token-protected, read tools only)
npx @ruvnet/ruview@0.9.1 mcp start
RUVIEW_MCP_GRANTS=device-access npx @ruvnet/ruview@0.9.1 mcp start --http

# Claude Code: a live sensing pane (/ruview), shipped in the package
npx @ruvnet/ruview@0.9.1 mod

# Run a read-only RuView agent through Codex
npx @ruvnet/ruview@0.9.1 agent run --host codex --repo . \
  --prompt "Find the nearest tests and cite the source files"

# Check claims, replay the deterministic proof, search the reviewed brain
npx @ruvnet/ruview@0.9.1 claim-check --file REPORT.md
npx @ruvnet/ruview@0.9.1 verify
npx @ruvnet/ruview@0.9.1 brain search --query "calibration"
```

**Safety:**
- Agent runs are read-only by default. Workspace writes require both `--allow-write` and `--confirm`.
- Hardware reads need the `device-access` grant.
- Flashing and calibration never run over the HTTP transport.
- Device-reported vitals are labelled as unvalidated.
- Retrieved brain content is evidence, not authority.

A single `npx ruview` package bundling all of this is ready (ADR-376). It is waiting on npm to release the unscoped name.

Full walkthrough: [user guide → RuView npm toolkit](docs/user-guide.md#ruview-npm-toolkit-ruvnetruview).

</details>

Built on [RuVector](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruvector/) and [Cognitum Seed](https://cognitum.one), RuView runs entirely on edge hardware — an ESP32 mesh (as low as $9 per node) paired with a Cognitum Seed for persistent memory, cryptographic attestation, and AI integration. No cloud, no cameras, no internet required.

The system learns each environment locally using spiking neural networks that adapt in under 30 seconds, with multi-frequency mesh scanning across 6 WiFi channels that uses your neighbors' routers as free radar illuminators. Every measurement is cryptographically attested via an Ed25519 witness chain.

RuView turns ordinary WiFi into a contactless sensor. A $9 ESP32 board reads the radio reflections off the people in a room, and a small pretrained model — published on Hugging Face at [`ruvnet/wifi-densepose-pretrained`](https://huggingface.co/ruvnet/wifi-densepose-pretrained) — tells you who's there, how they're breathing, and how their heart rate is trending. The model fits in 8 KB (4-bit quantized) and runs in microseconds on a Raspberry Pi. (The [v2 encoder](https://huggingface.co/ruvnet/wifi-densepose-pretrained) reports an honest, label-free held-out **temporal-triplet accuracy of 82.3%** — up from 66.4% raw; the older "100% presence" figure was measured on a single-class recording and has been retracted in favor of this.) No cameras, no wearables, no app on the user's phone.

### Built for low-power edge applications

[Edge modules](#edge-intelligence-adr-041) are small programs that run directly on the ESP32 sensor — no internet needed, no cloud fees, instant response.

> | 💓 **Heart rate** | Bandpass 0.8–2.0 Hz, zero-crossing BPM | 40–120 BPM, real-time |
> | 👤 **Presence detection** | Trained head on Hugging Face ([`ruvnet/wifi-densepose-pretrained`](https://huggingface.co/ruvnet/wifi-densepose-pretrained); v2 encoder = 82.3% held-out temporal-triplet acc, honestly re-benchmarked) + a phase-variance fallback that needs no model | < 1 ms, ~30 s ambient calibration |
> | 🧬 **CSI embeddings** | 128-dim contrastive encoder shipped on Hugging Face, 4-bit quantised variant fits in 8 KB | **164,183 emb/s** on M4 Pro |
> | 🦴 **17-keypoint pose estimation** | `cog-pose-estimation` Cog v0.0.1 — signed aarch64 + x86_64 binaries on GCS, loads `pose_v1.safetensors` via Candle (the committed `pose_v1` is a **first-cut** on-device model: PCK@20 = 3.0%, below the ADR-079 ≥35% target, and its runtime path is still a `confidence=0` stub — see [Model weights: what's real, what's not](#model-weights-whats-real-whats-not); the **82.69%** figure below is the separate published MM-Fi benchmark, not this live cog). Train your own from paired data in 2.1 s on an RTX 5080 ([ADR-101](docs/adr/ADR-101-pose-estimation-cog.md), [benchmarks](docs/benchmarks/pose-estimation-cog.md)). **SOTA on MM-Fi:** [`ruvnet/wifi-densepose-mmfi-pose`](https://huggingface.co/ruvnet/wifi-densepose-mmfi-pose) hits **82.69% torso-PCK@20** (ensemble 83.59%), beating MultiFormer (72.25%) and CSI2Pose (68.41%) on the matched MM-Fi `random_split` protocol — self-corrected and auditable on [AetherArena](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ruvnet/aether-arena) | 8.4 ms cold-start on a Pi 5 |

Six specialised learned counters available as Cogs: `occupancy-zones`, `elevator-count`, `queue-length`, `customer-flow`, `clean-room`, `person-matching` | Real-time, self-calibrating |
> | 🌍 **World model prediction** | OccWorld TransVQVAE — 15-frame future occupancy prediction, 209 ms inference, 3.4 GB VRAM on RTX 5080; fine-tune on your space with `occworld_retrain.py` ([ADR-147](docs/adr/ADR-147-nvidia-cosmos-world-foundation-model-integration.md)) | 15 frames × 200×200×16 vox |

## About

Concat is a free, open-source video editor for macOS, Windows, Linux and Android. It covers what most edits need: auto-captions, text-to-speech, background removal, keyframe animation, effects and titles, multi-track cutting, 4K export. With none of the catches: no watermark, no account, no subscription, no upload.

Everything runs locally on a native Rust engine with a GPU compositor. Install it, drop in footage, cut. The AI models for captions, voices and cutout download once from Settings and work offline after that. Your footage never leaves your disk.

**Good for:** TikTok, Reels and Shorts, YouTube videos, tutorials and screen recordings, podcast clips, memes.

**Also for machines:** a built-in MCP server for AI agents (`concat --mcp`, [set up](docs/MCP.md)) and a JSON-RPC API for scripts, so they can cut video with it too.

## Highlights

- 🚫 **No watermarks. No account. No paywall.** Ever.
- 🔒 **100% local.** Nothing uploads. Works offline.
- 💬 **Auto-captions.** Local Whisper. Pick a model size, get styled captions on the timeline.
- 🗣️ **Text-to-speech + voice cloning.** A free local voice on the desktop, or any voice from a few seconds of a recording. Phones are getting their own system voice.
- 🧍 **Background removal.** People, objects, or paint the mask yourself.
- 🎞️ **Keyframes.** Position, scale, rotation, opacity, volume, effect parameters. Curve editor built in.
- ✨ **100 effects, filters and transitions.** GPU-rendered, live in the preview.
- ✂️ **Cut fast.** Split, trim, ripple, merge, freeze frame, speed. Magnetic timeline if you want it.
- 🎚️ **Multi-track, multi-timeline.** Overlays and picture-in-picture: stack video, stills and titles on as many tracks as you like. Several cuts in one project. Blend modes (screen, add, multiply…), crop, flips.
- 📝 **Titles.** Fonts, stroke, shadow, background plate. Presets to start from.
- 🎙️ **One-switch voice cleanup.** Denoise, enhance voice, level the loudness. Plus chipmunk, robot, telephone and friends.
- 📤 **Export.** H.264, HEVC, AV1. Up to 4K 60, 10-bit colour.
- 🦀 **Native Rust engine.** GPU compositor, proxies, hardware decode. 4K scrubs smoothly.
- 🤖 **Scriptable.** An MCP server built in, so Claude and other AI agents can edit with it ([one line to set up](docs/MCP.md)), and a JSON-RPC API for scripts. A build from source adds gRPC and a command-line tool.
- 🖥️ **macOS, Windows, Linux, Android.** 26 languages. Same app, same project files.

## Download

Two ways in:

1. **[The website](https://concat.standalones.org/#download)** hands you the right build for your machine. Start here.
2. **[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/releases)** has every build for every platform, with installers, packages and checksums. For when you want to pick.

Concat is in **beta**: it works, and it still has edges. [Say so](https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/issues) when you find one.

**Platforms**

- ✅ **Windows** · x86_64 (ARM builds are paused, see [#326](https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/issues/326)). A setup and an `.msi`. If SmartScreen stops an unsigned build: **More info** › **Run anyway**
- ✅ **macOS** · Intel and Apple silicon. If macOS refuses to open an unsigned build: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Concat.app`
- ✅ **Linux** · x86_64 and ARM. `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.AppImage` and an Arch package. Also a Flatpak on **[Flatpark](https://flatpark.org/apps/app.concat.editor/)**, a community Flatpak remote that wraps the x86_64 `.deb` of each release and updates with it
- ✅ **Android** · phones and tablets
- ✅ **iOS / iPadOS** · iPhone and iPad, sideloaded

✅ Supported · 🚧 Work in progress · 🧪 To be tested

**System requirements** and the optional model sizes are on [the website](https://concat.standalones.org/guides/system-requirements).

**[Code signing policy](CODE_SIGNING.md)**: why the Windows builds are not signed yet, and what Concat sends over the network (nothing you did not ask for).

## Build from source

You need Rust 1.93 or newer (see `rust-version` in `src/Cargo.toml`), the FFmpeg 7+ development libraries, cmake and a C++ compiler.

- **macOS:** `brew install ffmpeg`
- **Windows:** from [FFmpeg's Windows downloads](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html#build-windows), take BtbN's `win64-gpl-shared` build (the one CI uses), unpack it and point `FFMPEG_DIR` at it
- **Linux:** use your distro's FFmpeg if it is version 7 or newer, otherwise use a BtbN `shared` build with `FFMPEG_DIR` like on Windows

Then:

```sh
cd src
cargo run -p concat          # the editor window
```

Other useful commands:

```sh
cargo build --profile app -p concat   # the shipping binary (fat LTO, stripped)
cargo test                            # run the test suite
cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings   # what CI checks
```

If you change text the interface shows, run `python3 scripts/locales.py` from the repo root so the string inventory stays in sync. Full details live in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

<h1 align="center">Open CAD Studio</h1>

<p align="center">
  Open-source 2D drafting and 3D modeling for desktop and web, built with Rust.
</p>

<p align="center">
  <a href="https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/releases/latest"><img alt="Latest release" src="https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio"></a>
  <a href="https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/releases"><img alt="Release downloads" src="https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/total"></a>
  <a href="https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/stargazers"><img alt="GitHub stars" src="https://img.shields.io/github/stars/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio"></a>

</p>

  <a href="https://www.opencadstudio.com"><strong>Launch the web app</strong></a>
  ·
  <a href="https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/releases/latest"><strong>Download the desktop app</strong></a>
  ·
  <a href="https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/discussions"><strong>Join the discussion</strong></a>
</p>

<p align="center">
  <img src="site/workspace.png" alt="Open CAD Studio workspace" width="100%">
</p>

## Overview

Open CAD Studio is a cross-platform application for technical drawing, layout work, and solid modeling. It reads and writes DWG and DXF drawings natively, with a shared editing core across the desktop and browser versions.

The experimental **IFCCAD** format choice exchanges supported CAD drawings in
`.ifccad` files. Existing `.ifcx` drawings remain readable. General IFCX BIM
models are not supported by this drawing route.
This alpha functionality is for testing only: later versions may not reopen
these files, and backward compatibility or migration is not guaranteed. Keep
original drawings and separate DWG/DXF copies. See the
[IFCCAD workflow and compatibility guide](docs/ifccad.md).

The project is under active development. Keep backups of important production drawings and report reproducible problems through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/issues).

## Highlights

- **Native drawing workflow** — open, edit, recover, and save DWG and DXF files without a conversion service.
- **Precise 2D drafting** — lines, polylines, curves, splines, hatches, object snaps, tracking, layers, blocks, and external references.
- **Documentation tools** — text, dimensions, leaders, tolerances, tables, model space, paper space, viewports, and plot styles.
- **Kernel-backed 3D modeling** — solid primitives, extrusion, revolution, sweep, loft, Boolean operations, and ACIS entity tessellation.
- **GPU rendering** — accelerated 2D and 3D viewports through `wgpu`, with orthographic and perspective cameras.
- **Extensible workflows** — native plugins, command scripts, headless conversion, and a line-based JSON automation API.

<p align="center">
  <img src="site/modeling.png" alt="3D model in Open CAD Studio" width="100%">
</p>

## File workflows

| Format or workflow | Support |
| --- | --- |
| DWG | Read and write; versioned save targets from R14 through 2018 |
| DXF | Read and write; versioned save targets from R14 through 2018 |
| BAK / SV$ | Open drawing backups and autosave files |
| OBJ | Import polygon meshes |
| SVG / SVGZ | Import vector shapes as a block (`SVGIN`, or `IMPORT`) |
| LandXML | Import `CgPoint` survey points |
| STL | Export 3D mesh data |
| STEP AP203 | Export 3D mesh data |
| PDF | Plot layouts and selected geometry on desktop |
| CSV | Extract entity property data |
| CTB / STB | Load and edit plot style tables |

## Desktop or web

Use the [web app](https://www.opencadstudio.com) for immediate access with no installation. Drawings are selected through the browser and saved as local downloads.

Use the desktop application for native file associations, file-manager thumbnails, system printing, PDF output, external plugins, command scripts, and headless automation. Release builds are available for Windows, Linux, and Apple Silicon macOS.

## Install

Download the package for your computer from the [download page](https://www.opencadstudio.com/download/); every link there is the latest release. All files are also on the [latest release](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/releases/latest) page.

### Windows

Choose one of these signed packages, `x86_64` for Intel and AMD processors or `arm64` for ARM processors:

- `OpenCADStudio-*-windows-x86_64-installer.msi` / `…-windows-arm64-installer.msi` — recommended installer with Start Menu shortcuts, DWG/DXF file associations, and drawing thumbnails.
- `OpenCADStudio-*-windows-x86_64-portable.exe` / `…-windows-arm64-portable.exe` — standalone application; no installation required.

Or install via Windows Package Manager:

```powershell
winget install HakanSeven.OpenCADStudio
```

### Linux

Download the AppImage (`linux-x86_64` or `linux-aarch64` for ARM), make it executable, and run it:

```bash
chmod +x OpenCADStudio-*-linux-x86_64.AppImage
./OpenCADStudio-*-linux-x86_64.AppImage
```

Or install it as a Flatpak from [FlatPark](https://flatpark.org/apps/io.github.HakanSeven12.OpenCadStudio), which installs the official AppImage and follows new releases:

```bash
flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists flatpark https://dl.flatpark.org/flatpark.flatpakrepo
flatpak install flatpark io.github.HakanSeven12.OpenCadStudio
```

The Flatpak opens and saves drawings through the file chooser. External references and underlays that point at other files need home access:

```bash
flatpak override --user --filesystem=home io.github.HakanSeven12.OpenCadStudio
```

Each release also carries a snap. It is not in the Snap Store yet, so snapd installs it only with `--dangerous`, and it does not update itself:

```bash
sudo snap install --dangerous OpenCADStudio-*-linux-x86_64.snap
```

### macOS

Packages are published for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs:

1. Download `OpenCADStudio-*-macos-arm64.dmg` (Apple Silicon) or `OpenCADStudio-*-macos-x86_64.dmg` (Intel).
2. Open the image and drag `OpenCADStudio.app` into **Applications**.
3. If Gatekeeper blocks the first launch, approve the app from **System Settings → Privacy & Security**.

The application is ad-hoc signed but is not currently notarized by Apple.

## Languages

Open CAD Studio can follow the system language or use any of these 23 interface languages:

> Arabic · Brazilian Portuguese · Bulgarian · Czech · Dutch · English · Finnish · French · German · Greek · Hindi · Hungarian · Italian · Japanese · Korean · Lao · Polish · Russian · Simplified Chinese · Spanish · Traditional Chinese · Turkish · Vietnamese

Change the language from the application settings. The browser version also uses the browser's preferred locale when **System** is selected.

## Build from source

### Desktop

Requirements:

- Git
- Current stable Rust toolchain
- Platform graphics and font development libraries

On Ubuntu or Debian, install the native dependencies with:

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install libgl1-mesa-dev libx11-dev libxcursor-dev libxi-dev \
  libxrandr-dev libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev libfontconfig1-dev \
  libfreetype6-dev
```

Then build and run:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio.git
cd OpenCADStudio
cargo build --release --bin OpenCADStudio
```

The resulting binary is written to `target/release/OpenCADStudio` (`OpenCADStudio.exe` on Windows).

### Web

Install the WebAssembly target and build tools once:

```bash
rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
cargo install trunk wasm-bindgen-cli
```

Start the development server:

```bash
trunk serve
```

## Automation

The desktop binary supports one-shot conversion, a persistent headless server, and a client-neutral MCP endpoint for AI applications:

```bash
OpenCADStudio --export input.dwg output.dxf
OpenCADStudio --export input-r12.dxf output.dwg --target-version R14
OpenCADStudio --serve
OpenCADStudio --serve --port 4242
OpenCADStudio --mcp
```

The automation server exchanges one JSON object per line over standard input/output or a local TCP socket. The self-contained MCP endpoint exposes the live desktop editor through the same tools to every compatible client. Its `audit` and `save_verified` operations check an explicit DWG/DXF target version, lossy records, raw DXF handle references, reopen the output, compare its semantic manifest, and return a SHA-256 hash. To connect a client, configure it to launch `OpenCADStudio --mcp`. See the [MCP control guide](docs/automation/README.md).

## Plugins

Desktop plugins run in separate processes and communicate with the host through the versioned plugin API. The browser build does not load native plugins.

- [Plugin architecture](docs/plugin-architecture.md)
- [Plugin template](docs/plugin-template/README.md)
- [Plugin registry](plugins/README.md)

## Project documentation

- [Automation API](docs/automation/README.md)
- [Plugin architecture](docs/plugin-architecture.md)
- [Tessellation pipeline](docs/tessellation.md)
- [Security policy](SECURITY.md)

## Contributing

Bug reports, focused pull requests, translations, documentation improvements, and plugin contributions are welcome.

- Search existing [issues](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/issues) before opening a new report.
- Use [Discussions](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/discussions) for questions and ideas.
- Report vulnerabilities privately by following the [security policy](SECURITY.md).

Application translations live in `locales/*/opencadstudio.ftl`; source labels map through
`src/locale_catalog.rs`. After editing translations, run `python3 scripts/export-locales.py`
to refresh web and desktop packaging labels. Validate with `python3 scripts/test_site.py`
and `cargo test --lib i18n::tests`.

## Project growth

### Stars

<a href="https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/stargazers">
  <picture>
    <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://www.opencadstudio.com/star-history-dark.svg">
    <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" srcset="https://www.opencadstudio.com/star-history-light.svg">
    <img alt="Open CAD Studio star history" src="https://www.opencadstudio.com/star-history-light.svg">
  </picture>
</a>

### Release downloads

<a href="https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/releases">
  <picture>
    <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://www.opencadstudio.com/download-history-dark.svg">

</a>

## Support the project

If Open CAD Studio helps your work, support continued development through [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/HakanSeven12) or [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/HakanSeven12).

# Universal Android Debloater Next Generation

> [!warning]
> **DISCLAIMER**: Use at your own risk. We're not responsible for anything that could happen to your devices.

<div align=center>
<img width=75% alt="screenshot of apps view" src=./resources/screenshots/v1.0.2.png>
</div>

This is a detached fork of the [UAD project](https://github.com/0x192/universal-android-debloater). This aims to improve privacy and efficiency (energy, speed, memory) by removing unnecessary and obscure system apps.
This can also improve security by reducing the [attack surface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_surface). Read [the wiki](https://github.com/Universal-Debloater-Alliance/universal-android-debloater-next-generation/wiki) for more details.

## Documentation

Everything about UAD-ng (and related stuff) can be found on the Wiki, such as:

- [Getting started](https://github.com/Universal-Debloater-Alliance/universal-android-debloater-next-generation/wiki/Getting-started)
- Features of this app
- [Usage guide](https://github.com/Universal-Debloater-Alliance/universal-android-debloater-next-generation/wiki/Usage)
- Suggested Android app replacements
- How to get the cutting-edge version by [building the source-code](https://github.com/Universal-Debloater-Alliance/universal-android-debloater-next-generation/wiki/Building-from-source)
- Weird things OEMs do
- [Suggested apps for analyzing APKs](https://github.com/Universal-Debloater-Alliance/universal-android-debloater-next-generation/wiki/How-to-contribute#useful-apps)

## Privacy

UAD-ng does not collect or transmit any user data. The only external connections are `GET` requests to GitHub for fetching the [package list](https://github.com/Universal-Debloater-Alliance/universal-android-debloater-next-generation/blob/main/resources/assets/uad_lists.json) ([crates/uad-core/src/uad_lists.rs](crates/uad-core/src/uad_lists.rs)) and checking for updates ([crates/uad-core/src/update.rs](crates/uad-core/src/update.rs)).

## Contact

**For real-time communication and support, consider joining our Discord guild:**

[<img width=64em alt="Discord symbol" src=./resources/images/icon_clyde_blurple.svg>](https://discord.gg/CzwbMCPEZa)

**If you prefer using Matrix, we have a bridge to Discord:**

[<img width=64em src=https://matrix.org/images/matrix-favicon.svg>](https://matrix.to/#/#uad-ng:matrix.org)

## Friends

Several projects integrate with or depend on UAD-ng's data and tools:

- **[Canta](https://github.com/samolego/Canta)** — A mobile Android debloater that uses Shizuku for rootless privilege escalation. It integrates with UAD-ng's Universal Debloat List to provide safe package recommendations without requiring a PC.

- **Projects by [Muntashir Akon](https://github.com/MuntashirAkon):**
  - **[AppManager](https://github.com/MuntashirAkon/AppManager)** — An advanced Android app manager with powerful debloating features.
  - **[android-debloat-list](https://github.com/MuntashirAkon/android-debloat-list)** — A comprehensive, community-driven list of Android packages to debloat, based on UAD-ng's list.
- **[De-Bloater](https://github.com/sunilpaulmathew/De-Bloater)** — An application using the power of Magisk to debloat unwanted system apps!

## Special thanks

- [@0x192](https://github.com/0x192) who created the original UAD project.
- [@mawilms](https://github.com/mawilms) for his LotRO plugin manager ([Lembas](https://github.com/mawilms/lembas)) which helped a lot to understand how to use the [Iced](https://github.com/iced-rs/iced) GUI library.
- [@casperstorm](https://github.com/casperstorm) for the UI/UX inspiration.

crmne/spotifast

Spotify, native and fast. One lightweight Rust app for your whole library, local playback, and Spotify Connect on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

Language: Rust

Stars: 10,075

Forks: 592

Stars today: 86 stars today

README

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/assets/images/logo.svg" alt="Spotifast logo" width="88" height="88">
</p>

<h1 align="center">Spotifast</h1>

<p align="center"><strong>Spotify, native and fast.</strong><br>A lightweight music app for Linux, macOS, and Windows.</p>

<p align="center">
  <a href="https://spotifast.rocks/download/"><strong>Download</strong></a> ·
  <a href="https://spotifast.rocks/getting-started/">Getting started</a> ·
  <a href="https://spotifast.rocks/using-spotifast/">User guide</a> ·
  <a href="CONTRIBUTING.md">Contribute</a>
</p>

<p align="center">
  <a href="Cargo.toml"><img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/Built_with-Rust-1ed760" alt="Built with Rust"></a>
  <a href="https://spotifast.rocks/download/"><img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/Linux_%C2%B7_macOS_%C2%B7_Windows-24292f" alt="Linux, macOS, and Windows"></a>
  <a href="LICENSE"><img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-1ed760" alt="MIT license"></a>
</p>

Spotifast is a Spotify client written in Rust with
[egui](https://www.egui.rs) and [fastframe](https://fastframe.dev), the
framework behind a family of native desktop apps. It plays music through
[Spotify Soloist](https://spotifast.rocks/soloist/) or the built-in
[librespot](https://github.com/librespot-org/librespot) player, and has no browser engine.

The interface includes complete
[translations for all supported languages](docs/_reference/translating.md#languages-and-coverage).

**Playback needs Spotify Premium.** Free accounts can browse and search, but
cannot play music through Spotifast.

![Spotifast Home with the playlist library, recommendations, queue, and player visible](docs/screenshot.png)

<details>
<summary><strong>Watch Spotifast in action</strong></summary>

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a5f669ce-b3b7-4f8e-9933-976a78876c7e

</details>

[Features](#your-music-on-your-desktop) · [Install](#install) · [First playback](#start-listening) · [Mini player](#the-winamp-mini-player) · [MilkDrop](#music-in-motion) · [Help](#guides-and-help)

Since 0.15, setup leads with Spotify's
[Soloist player](https://spotifast.rocks/soloist/), with guided key setup,
one-time pairing and automatic renewal of expiring builds. New listeners and
people updating see this choice once after sign-in on supported platforms.
**Use the built-in player** keeps librespot, with Spotifast's EQ, visualizers,
local files and full queue editing. The choice is remembered.
On Linux with PipeWire, Soloist also supports Spotifast’s EQ and visualizers
through a private audio route. [Native audio support](https://spotifast.rocks/soloist/#native-audio)
adds EQ and visualizers on macOS 14.2 or newer, and visualizers on Windows 11,
including MilkDrop. Windows Soloist playback does not support audible EQ.
The Mac route keeps Soloist at full volume after redirecting its output,
then applies Spotifast’s volume after the visualizers, including mute. Phone
volume changes adjust that output level; Spotify’s indicator returns to 100%.
Windows visuals keep their level as Soloist’s volume falls and stop only when it is muted.
When enabled, Soloist appears as **This computer**; settings show the controls
that apply to it. Turning it off restores the built-in player's preferences.
While Soloist starts and its account is verified, the Spotify loading screen shows
**Verifying Soloist…** and waits to accept playback commands. Setup takes three
steps, and ends with choosing the named device in Spotify, with the built-in
player available as a quiet alternative below the card. If Soloist stops later,
a banner over the app says so while Spotifast restarts it, and offers **Try
again** if that does not work. **Settings → Spotify Soloist → Spotify access**
connects the separate Spotify session for Made for you, listening activity and
Spotify lyrics without changing players.

## Your music, on your desktop

| Feature | What you can do |
|---|---|
| **Library and search** | Browse playlists, Liked Songs, albums, artists, and podcasts. Discover upcoming albums on artist pages and open their countdown to pre-save. Search the catalogue and edit playlists you own. Copy a song's link, title, or artists from its menu. |
| **Local files** | Play the local files your playlists list from a folder you choose in Settings, at any sample rate. Names show spaces and accents correctly, including in cached playlists. |
| **Lyrics** | Spotify lyrics when the playback session is signed in, with LRCLIB as fallback. Temporary LRCLIB overloads retry and try search; older cached lyrics remain available during outages. |
| **Spotify Connect** | Play on this computer or control playback on your other devices, including Google Cast speakers and groups. Cast devices appear as they are discovered; frequently and recently chosen outputs rise to the top. Remote volume keeps your chosen level while Spotify updates. |
| **Queue** | Add songs to the queue, or choose **Play next** to put a song or selection first when playing on this computer. |
| **Themes** | Choose light, dark, system appearance, or custom colours, with one theme for light mode and one for dark mode that switch with the system. On Omarchy, follow your desktop theme. |
| **Desktop controls** | Use keyboard shortcuts and media keys. Keep music playing from the tray when supported by your desktop and settings, and start Spotifast with your computer, with its window or in the tray. |
| **Winamp mini player** | Use classic skins with an equalizer, playlist, and animated sound displays. |
| **MilkDrop** | Watch music-reactive visuals in a separate window or full screen. See platform availability below. |

## Install

| Platform | Installation |
|---|---|
| **macOS** | `brew install --cask crmne/tap/spotifast`, or [download the Mac app](https://spotifast.rocks/download/#macos). |
| **Arch Linux** | `yay -S spotifast-bin` |
| **Windows** | The installer or a portable ZIP, for x64 and ARM, from the [Download page](https://spotifast.rocks/download/#windows). |
| **Debian, Ubuntu** | The [DEB package](https://spotifast.rocks/download/#debian-and-ubuntu), then `sudo apt install ./spotifast_*.deb` |
| **Fedora** | The [RPM package](https://spotifast.rocks/download/#fedora), then `sudo dnf install ./spotifast-*.rpm` |
| **Other Linux** | Find Flatpak, AppImage, Nix, and other options on the [Download page](https://spotifast.rocks/download/#linux). |
| **From source** | Follow [Build from source](https://spotifast.rocks/getting-started/#build-from-source) for dependencies and commands. |

## Start listening

1. Register Spotifast with Spotify, as the sign-in screen shows: in the
   [Spotify developer dashboard](https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard),
   click **Create app**, Spotify's name for this registration, with the
   redirect URI `http://127.0.0.1:8989/login` and **Web API** ticked. It takes
   about two minutes and gives you a Client ID. Spotify requires Premium on the
   account that registers, so a Free account can't do this step itself.
   [Getting started](https://spotifast.rocks/getting-started/#make-a-spotify-app)
   has the steps.
2. Paste the Client ID into Spotifast and choose **Sign in with Spotify**.
   Approve access in your browser, then return to the app to see your library.
3. To listen on this computer, open the device menu in the bottom player bar
   and choose **Set up playback here**, also available in Settings.
4. Complete the separate playback approval in your browser. Your computer
   appears as a Spotify Connect device named **Spotifast**.

Library access and local playback have separate approvals. Spotifast remembers
both using your computer's protected storage. See
[Getting started](https://spotifast.rocks/getting-started/) for the full walkthrough
and [How it connects](https://spotifast.rocks/how-it-connects/) for the details.

## The Winamp mini player

A classic look for your music, with Winamp 2 `.wsz` and Windows Media Player `.wmz` skins, an equalizer,
a playlist, and animated sound displays. Switch with **Ctrl+M**
(**Cmd+Shift+M** on macOS), the shrink button, or Settings.
The spectrum analyser and oscilloscope also work in the collapsed title bar.

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/assets/images/winamp.png" alt="Spotifast's Winamp mini player with the built-in skin, equalizer, and playlist" width="320">
</p>

[Explore the mini player](https://spotifast.rocks/winamp/), including skins,
window sizes, controls, and the return to the main player.

## Music in motion

MilkDrop reacts to music playing on this computer, with more than 10,000
presets downloaded on first use. Open it from the visualiser button,
Settings, or the mini player's **V** menu.

![MilkDrop visualiser displaying coloured concentric patterns in Spotifast](docs/assets/images/milkdrop-poster.jpg)

Included on **Linux**, **macOS**, and **Windows Intel/AMD** builds.
It is not included in the Windows on ARM download.
[Read the MilkDrop guide](https://spotifast.rocks/milkdrop/) for presets,
controls, and fullscreen mode.

## Guides and help

The complete guide lives at **[spotifast.rocks](https://spotifast.rocks/)**.

| You want to… | Read |
|---|---|
| Sign in, set up playback, or configure themes, fonts, and proxies | [Getting started](https://spotifast.rocks/getting-started/) |
| Learn shortcuts, command-line controls, and updates | [Everyday use](https://spotifast.rocks/using-spotifast/) |
| Check storage sizes, clear cached audio and find stored files | [Settings and files](https://spotifast.rocks/settings-and-files/) |
| Understand scrolling performance and reduce loading delays | [Make it even faster](https://spotifast.rocks/make-it-even-faster/) |
| Fix "Spotify refused the audio key" or "Spotify is being slow" | [When something goes wrong](https://spotifast.rocks/troubleshooting/) |
| Understand what is stored and sent | [Privacy](https://spotifast.rocks/privacy/) · [How it connects](https://spotifast.rocks/how-it-connects/) |
| Check Spotify and librespot limitations | [What Spotify allows](https://spotifast.rocks/what-spotify-allows/) |
| Is it safe for my account? | [Account safety](https://spotifast.rocks/what-is-spotifast/#account-safety) |
| Report a bug or propose a feature | Read [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md), then use the [issue forms](https://github.com/crmne/spotifast/issues/new/choose). |

## Contributing

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening an issue or pull
request. To look at the interface without a Spotify account, run:

```sh
cargo run --features demo -- --demo
```

Translations live in `assets/i18n/`; see
[Translating Spotifast](docs/_reference/translating.md). Release packaging
is described in [PACKAGING.md](PACKAGING.md).

## More native apps

**Want WhatsApp just as fast and native?** [ZapFast](https://zapfast.rocks)
is Spotifast's sibling. Both are built on
[fastframe](https://fastframe.dev).

## Spotify Connect updates

With local playback enabled, Spotify pushes changes from other devices over
Spotifast's existing Connect session. Playback changes trigger a refresh.
Volume-only changes appear directly for the active playback device without
an extra request; an unconfirmed volume change made in Spotifast takes
precedence. Push-triggered refreshes are at least a second apart and wait for
a pending playback read to finish. Changes received during that read are
folded into one follow-up.
Connect pushes are ignored when this computer is the active device both
before and after; position-only updates cause no requests. Regular polling
remains the fallback.

## Sonos playback

Sonos speakers use the Spotify Connect session for playback control. Enable
local playback first, then select the speaker in the device picker.

## Acknowledgements

Spotifast uses [librespot](https://github.com/librespot-org/librespot),
[egui](https://www.egui.rs), [fastframe](https://fastframe.dev), the [Inter](https://rsms.me/inter/)
typeface (OFL), and [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) icons (ISC).

Spotifast is an independent project and is not affiliated with Spotify.
Spotify is a trademark of Spotify AB.

Licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

    <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://api.star-history.com/chart?repos=crmne/spotifast&type=date&theme=dark">
    <img alt="Spotifast GitHub stars over time" src="https://api.star-history.com/chart?repos=crmne/spotifast&type=date">

# AIVPN

[![CI](https://github.com/infosave2007/aivpn/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=master)](https://github.com/infosave2007/aivpn/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

---

## Overview

AIVPN combines UDP tunnel encryption with traffic masking. Masks define the outer protocol, packet sizes and send intervals. Being recognized as STUN or QUIC does not by itself prove statistical indistinguishability from a specific application.

Key technical properties:

- **InitialV2 and PFS** - the initial exchange confirms a fresh server key; data and management commands travel only after PFS. Bound and privileged devices must also prove their persistent key and, when mTLS is required, present a valid certificate.
- **O(1) session lookup** — no session ID is transmitted in the clear. Every packet carries an 8-byte *resonance tag* derived from a timestamp and a per-session secret. The server resolves the session in constant time via a `DashMap`.
- **Perfect Forward Secrecy** — in-flight session key rotation via X25519 ratchet. Compromising the server key does not expose past traffic.
- **Neural Resonance module** — per-mask micro-MLP (~66 KB) monitors live traffic statistics; high reconstruction error triggers automatic mask rotation without disconnecting clients.
- **Generative mask distributions** - profiles support multimodal packet-size and inter-arrival models fitted from captured traffic with a BIC-selected Gaussian mixture. Clients sample the stored model; its presence does not establish similarity to a named application.
- **Written in Rust** — memory-safe, no GC pauses. Client binary ≈ 2.5 MB. Runs on a $5 VPS.

---

## Architecture

### Workspace layout

```
crates/aivpn-common/     — shared crypto, protocol, mask profiles (no I/O)
crates/aivpn-server/     — Linux-only VPN gateway and management CLI
crates/aivpn-client/     — cross-platform VPN client (Linux / macOS / Windows)
crates/aivpn-android-core/ — JNI bridge for Android (Rust → Kotlin via C FFI)
crates/aivpn-ios-core/   — iOS Rust staticlib (C FFI), linked by PacketTunnelProvider
crates/aivpn-windows/    — Windows GUI (egui/eframe 0.31, manages aivpn-client.exe subprocess)
crates/aivpn-linux/      - Linux GUI (Iced 0.14, wraps aivpn-client subprocess)
platforms/android/       — Android Kotlin app (MVVM: MainViewModel + RecyclerView)
platforms/ios/           — iOS SwiftUI app + NetworkExtension PacketTunnelProvider
platforms/macos/         — macOS SwiftUI menu bar app + privileged helper daemon
platforms/aivpn-web/     — Web management panel (Hono 4 + SvelteKit 2, SQLite/PostgreSQL)
platforms/linux/         — Linux desktop packaging (AppImage, .desktop)
platforms/linux-kernel/  — optional in-kernel data-path module (out-of-tree)
platforms/openwrt/       — OpenWrt package
platforms/mikrotik/      — MikroTik RouterOS container
assets/masks/            — bundled traffic mimicry JSON profiles
assets/brand/            — icons and brand material
deploy/                  — server installer, systemd unit, Dockerfiles
deploy/ci/               — CI gates run by the Makefile (see `make help`)
```

### Key modules

| Module | Location | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| `crypto.rs` | `aivpn-common` | X25519 key exchange, ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD, BLAKE3/HMAC, resonance tag generation |
| `protocol.rs` | `aivpn-common` | Wire format: `[8-byte tag][pad_len][inner_header][encrypted payload][poly1305 tag]` |
| `mask.rs` | `aivpn-common` | `MaskProfile` — traffic shaping: header templates, FSM states, IAT distributions |
| `gateway.rs` | `aivpn-server` | Central event loop: UDP receive, session dispatch, NAT forwarding, neural checks |
| `session.rs` | `aivpn-server` | `SessionManager` — `DashMap`-based O(1) tag lookup, 256-entry replay window, 500-session cap |
| `neural.rs` | `aivpn-server` | Neural Resonance: per-mask MLP 64→16→64 / fallback 64→128→64, MSE threshold 0.35, auto mask rotation |
| `client.rs` | `aivpn-client` | State machine: Unprovisioned → Connecting → Connected, key exchange, reconnection |
| `tunnel.rs` | `aivpn-client` | Cross-platform TUN: `/dev/net/tun` (Linux), `utun` (macOS), Wintun (Windows) |
| `mimicry.rs` | `aivpn-client` | `MimicryEngine` — applies `MaskProfile` to outbound packets |

### Initial exchange and accelerator compatibility

Starting with 1.2.0, the initial exchange uses InitialV2. It is incompatible with 1.1.0 and earlier 1.2.0 development builds. Update servers, pool/site/chain nodes and all clients together, including embedded mobile cores. The connection key format and the inter-server management protocol are unchanged. The initial AEAD uses XChaCha20-Poly1305 with a random 24-byte nonce and the connection context in the AAD; the established channel keeps the existing ChaCha20-Poly1305 format and kernel ABI 7.

The Linux module requires compatible Rust-for-Linux APIs, kernel headers built with `CONFIG_RUST=y` and the matching Rust toolchain. A kernel version number alone does not guarantee support. Before registering `/dev/aivpn`, the module checks `file_operations.owner` in the real miscdevice vtable and fails with `ENODEV` if the API does not pin the module code to the open descriptor. This check cannot be bypassed; without the accelerator, userspace TUN is used.

### Mask state and outer traffic validation

The QUIC mask runs bidirectional QUIC v1/TLS 1.3: it keeps CIDs and packet numbers and handles ACKs, loss, timers and connection close. The engine runs inside the shared mask layer on top of the existing UDP/DatagramTransport. A cold Initial carries an empty Token. The initial AIVPN packet travels inside an encrypted HTTP DATAGRAM after TLS, HTTP/3 SETTINGS and CONNECT-UDP; until then payload data waits in a bounded queue. When the local buffer is full, the client waits for free space while it keeps processing ACKs and control messages. The logical UDP peer terminates inside the mask; no proxy sockets are opened. A plain GET and an unrelated CONNECT-UDP receive HTTP 403. CONNECT-UDP is not equivalent to ordinary HTTP/3 requests to Avito or VK Video and does not by itself prove similarity to them. Before inner authentication the server keeps a separate bounded TLS state that grants no VPN access and cannot replace an active session. Up to 128 such states are allowed globally, at most two per UDP peer, with at most ten seconds to complete setup; processing is charged to a shared CPU budget. Until the address is validated, responses are limited to three times the received traffic. TLS verifies the handshake signature and possession of the certificate key, but not the public PKI: trust in the server comes from the inner signed AIVPN exchange. 0-RTT and connection migration are disabled.

The pre-authentication inbound packet limit is set by the server's `--per-ip-pps-limit` / `AIVPN_PER_IP_PPS_LIMIT`, 5000 packets per second per IP by default. The current QUIC generation with an admitted PFS session has a separate finite limit, `--per-ip-authenticated-pps-limit` / `AIVPN_PER_IP_AUTHENTICATED_PPS_LIMIT`, 100000 by default. Queues and counters for the two classes are bounded independently; pending TLS, plain and RTC traffic keep the first limit. The CID selects the route and quota but does not authenticate the packet: Quinn AEAD and the inner AIVPN checks remain mandatory, including for a known CID.

Seven profiles open the exchange with an aligned optional STUN Binding Indication attribute. After PFS, the protected `MaskState` message binds the outer protocol parameters to the profile and connection generation. Zoom and `webrtc_yandex_telemost_v1` use ICE/DTLS/SRTP; SberJazz and Telegram calls add TURN Allocate, Permission, ChannelBind and ChannelData. WhatsApp uses ICE/SRTP without DTLS, with separate per-direction keys from the protected exchange. Keys, ICE credentials and certificates are created anew for each generation. All states run in the shared mask layer on top of the existing UDP socket; queues and setup time are bounded. VK Teams and Salute still use a limited STUN carrier. Mask names and a correct outer protocol do not guarantee indistinguishability from a specific application. Older external signed profiles with a 20-byte header must be reissued; the client does not modify signed data automatically.

The `telegram_calls_v1` profile targets Telegram UDP calls, not MTProto. The former `telegram_mtproto_v1`, which wrongly used QUIC, is removed from the catalog. Explicit mask selections must replace its ID; the old ID is not an alias of the new one. TURN/ICE/DTLS/SRTP reproduce the observed media-channel stages, but not Telegram's signaling protocol.

The `yandex_alice_v1` profile is temporarily excluded from the bundled catalog and installation bundle. The voice RPC of the verified Alice mobile app uses TLS/TCP rather than the current STUN/UDP carrier. The smart speaker protocol has not been verified separately.

The client picks size and IAT as one pair and schedules data without blocking control messages. The server uses a separate bounded queue per session and the reverse profile parameters when one is defined. In both directions IP flows are interleaved while each flow keeps its packet order: a large background transfer does not fill the whole queue ahead of DNS and new connections.

`adaptive` is the default. For QUIC, the protocol's own congestion control and pacer set the rate; no second per-IP-packet IAT timer is added. For other masks, light load keeps the profile intervals; persistent queueing delay gradually raises the rate, which returns to the original once the backlog clears. The controller tracks the age of the oldest packet and the minimum of that age over a 100 ms window. A delay above 5 ms raises the rate 1.5x per window; below 1 ms the rate returns toward the original with a factor of 0.8. Acceleration is capped at 4096x. Short accelerated intervals are merged into a 1 ms quantum limited to 64 original IP packets; after a delay, old quanta give no credit. Fragmentation may produce more outer frames. An expired deadline is processed immediately; a future one keeps waiting. A profile change resets the controller. This is local queue regulation, not a measurement of physical link capacity.

`full` mode keeps the original intervals under any load. Client `off` disables pauses while keeping padding and the mask format. Server `off` also disables padding, as before; server `light` caps the delay at two milliseconds and keeps a small padding budget. In `adaptive`, padding is unchanged, but intervals under load differ from the original profile. Preserving the format and encryption does not by itself prove resistance to DPI. Padding enlarges short packets but does not shrink long ones: the sizes and rate of the real workload limit how closely the profile can be matched.

The policy is set locally and is not imported from the connection key:

- Client: `"upload_shaping": "adaptive"`, `"full"` or `"off"` in the shared `config.json`; the CLI also reads this field from an explicitly selected `--config`. With an explicit `--config`, the default file is not merged with it. On Linux the default path is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/aivpn/config.json` or `$HOME/.config/aivpn/config.json`, falling back to `/etc/aivpn/config.json` when neither directory exists. A client started through sudo or a service uses that process's environment. Windows uses `%APPDATA%/aivpn/config.json` with the `C:\ProgramData\aivpn\config.json` fallback; macOS and iOS use `$HOME/Library/Application Support/aivpn/config.json`. Android uses the app's `filesDir/config.json`, including for direct UDP.
- Server: `"downlink_shaping": "adaptive"` in `server.json` or `--shaping-level adaptive`. `full`, `light`, `off` and legacy booleans remain supported: `true` means `full`, `false` means `off`. Explicit settings are not changed by an upgrade.

Restart the client process or the server service to apply a new setting. An invalid value is a configuration error, not a silent fallback to the default mode.

On Linux, a full tunnel without an assigned IPv6 address blocks IPv6 with two owned blackhole routes, including when the IPv4 MTU is below 1280. With an assigned IPv6 address, the interface MTU is never below 1280. An explicit disconnect removes the owned routes; after a crash, `aivpn-client kill-switch clear` removes the firewall rules and any remaining owned IPv6 guards. Leftover IPv6 routes are not cleaned up automatically on a normal start: only an explicit operator command removes them. Update the CLI and `aivpn-ip-helper` from the same build.

All 10 bundled profiles are available through `--preferred-mask` and `--polymorphic-base`; an unknown ID is rejected. The preference selects an initial candidate of the requested base from the verified bootstrap. If there is no such candidate, the client keeps the trusted opening and requests the base after PFS. `--polymorphic-base` takes precedence; later automatic server rotations still apply. Retries of the initial exchange keep the ephemeral key of a single attempt but use a fresh nonce. The whole attempt is limited to 10 seconds. Switching between the STUN and QUIC mask families does not require a new session. Outer QUIC and SRTP packets are limited to 1380 bytes; QUIC starts at 1200 UDP bytes and probes the path MTU up to 1380. The inner packet is limited to 1140 bytes for QUIC, 1324 for ICE/DTLS/SRTP and 1358 for ICE/SRTP. Padding accounts for the headers, AEAD and alignment of the selected carrier. Control messages are fragmented before encryption. QUIC and RTC run in userspace in both directions, and plain STUN TX also stays in userspace; ABI 7 is unchanged. Native installation and systemd stay the same.

The default TUN MTU is 1280 bytes; an explicit TUN MTU up to 1500 is preserved. Inner DATA and FEC repairs that exceed the carrier budget are authenticated and fragmented separately, then reassembled at the receiver. FEC counts each original IP packet once. A peer must support the 1.2.0 fragment format. Every FEC member carries an authenticated group number and position, including small packets. Groups remain separate across reordering and an FEC pause; completed groups reject late originals before fragment allocation. FEC frames use the userspace receive path even when FEC was enabled after a kernel session was installed.

The new QUIC mask format and bundled STUN profile versions require clients and servers to be updated together, including pool/site/chain nodes and mobile cores. The connection key format, PSK and inter-server management messages are unchanged. `make mask-gate` runs the real client and gateway over UDP with loss, delay and duplicates, verifies PFS and the reverse exchange, then parses bidirectional PCAPs with TShark and nDPI, checking the first packets separately. This validates structure and classification; it does not prove resistance to arbitrary DPI or active probing.

### Pool sync

Server-to-server client database synchronization uses `ControlPayload::PoolSync` carried inside ordinary VPN UDP packets — indistinguishable from client traffic. No separate TCP port or firewall rule required.

---

## Platform Support

| Platform | Server | Client | GUI | TUN driver |
|----------|:------:|:------:|:---:|------------|
| Linux CLI | ✅ | ✅ | — | `/dev/net/tun` |
| Linux GUI | — | ✅ | ✅ iced AppImage + tray | `/dev/net/tun` |

| Android | — | ✅ | ✅ native Kotlin | `VpnService` API |
| iOS | — | ✅ | ✅ SwiftUI | `NetworkExtension` |
| MikroTik RouterOS 7.6+ | — | ✅ | — | container veth + TUN |
| Entware routers (ARMv7 / MIPSel) | — | ✅ | — | musl static binary |

OOOSplat 是一款将普通或全景视频、图片序列一键转换为 3D Gaussian Splatting 的本地桌面应用。选择素材、项目目录和质量档位，即可自动完成生成，并直接预览、编辑和导出结果。

Windows 和 Apple Silicon macOS Alpha 均随应用提供 FFmpeg、FFprobe、COLMAP 和 Brush；Linux 支持目前仅作为 Ubuntu 24.04 LTS x86_64 Alpha 提供。整个生成流程使用本机 CPU 和 GPU，输入素材、工程文件、模型与日志无需上传到云端重建或训练服务。React 界面通过 Tauri 直接调用本机 Rust 后端，普通生成与预览不需要额外启动 HTTP 服务。

查看 [OOOSplat Roadmap](ROADMAP.md) 了解后续规划。

> 0.7.1 更新默认生成、自动重试与精细档预算，加入分级抽帧和漫游调速，完善补拍、图片 GPS 辅助、导出及错误诊断。

以下以当前 `main` 源码功能为准，安装包内容以对应版本说明为准。

## 核心优势

- **一键生成高斯泼溅**：只需选择输入视频或图片序列、项目目录和质量档位，即可自动完成画面准备、COLMAP 相机重建、Brush 训练和 `final.ply` 发布，无需手动拼接命令或配置引擎。
- **全平台兼容**：支持 Windows、macOS 和 Linux，可在三大主流桌面系统上完成本地高斯泼溅生成；具体系统与处理器要求请参阅下方兼容性说明。
- **安全与隐私保护**：素材、抽帧、相机重建数据、高斯模型和日志默认只保存在用户选择的本地项目目录，核心生成流程在本机完成，无需将原始视频、图像或模型上传到第三方重建与训练平台，从而减少数据在网络传输、云端留存和未经授权访问过程中的泄露风险。
- **完全本地化算力**：重建与训练均在用户自己的电脑上运行，不调用远程计算服务。满足要求时 COLMAP 自动使用本机 NVIDIA GPU 加速，否则回退 CPU，过程和数据始终由用户掌控。

## 展示视频

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b9e8cef-4c71-4bfa-ba23-641fcdd37659

## 界面预览

### 创建与管理任务

![OOOSplat 创建新任务与任务列表界面](assets/screenshots/task-workspace.png)

### 高斯泼溅预览与调整

![OOOSplat 高斯泼溅预览与 Transform 调整界面](assets/screenshots/gaussian-preview.png)

## 主要功能

- **一键生成**：支持 MP4、MOV 和 JPG、JPEG、PNG 图片序列，自动完成画面准备、相机重建、训练和 PLY 发布。
- **全景素材**：支持已拼接、单目、完整 360°×180° 的 2:1 ERP MP4 和图片文件夹；自动检测类型，无法确定时在素材框中选择。
- **图片顺序确认**：普通及全景图片超过100张时，生成前询问拍摄顺序；已排序使用顺序匹配，未排序或100张及以下使用穷举匹配。
- **图片 GPS**：识别内嵌定位信息，在通过校验的 Windows x64 路径中辅助匹配与重建，可靠时提供北向与米制尺度；信息不足自动沿用原流程。[范围及验证](docs/IMAGE_GPS.md)
- **导入外部模型**：可从“已完成”分组导入标准/压缩 PLY、SOG、SPZ、SPLAT 和 KSPLAT；完整 COLMAP 数据会自动关联，通过兼容性校验后可补拍，外部文件保持只读。
- **三种质量档位**：默认启用重建优化与自动补帧，视频可分级调整抽帧比例，手动比例任务最多额外补20%；精细档保留原始训练分辨率，普通素材按有效像素与重建轨迹计算 Splat 上限（系数0.5），全景保持独立预算。
- **自动重试**：默认开启，允许显存不足后减少点数重试或调整补拍方案；可关闭，实际重试后在完成详情标记。
- **透明素材**：支持透明 MOV 和 PNG，保留原始颜色与 Alpha，并自动生成 COLMAP 黑白蒙版。
- **多任务管理**：任务列表分为新任务、已完成和未完成，可保存多个草稿、调整顺序并自动执行下一个任务；同一时间只运行一个生成任务，支持取消和断点续跑。
- **补拍**：根据原模型情况选择重建方式及是否沿用原模型，训练参数与正常生成一致；支持跨尺寸普通素材和完整 ERP 全景补拍，派生项目不覆盖原结果。
- **预览与编辑**：支持 WebGPU／WebGL2、移动轴与旋转环、裁切、删点、反选和撤销重做；静止画面停止重绘，交互最高60 FPS。支持0.1×–5.0×水平 WASD 漫游与首帧训练视角定位。
- **多种导出**：支持标准 PLY、压缩 PLY、SPZ v4、单文件 SOG，以及竖屏或横屏 MP4、单文件离线 HTML。SPZ 坐标越界时，经确认可仅调整导出副本。
- **本地运行**：COLMAP 重建与 Brush 训练都在本机完成；满足条件时自动使用 GPU，否则使用可用的兼容路径。
- **跨平台与双语界面**：支持 Windows、Apple Silicon macOS 和 Ubuntu，并可在简体中文与英文之间切换。

全景图片每批需至少两张且尺寸一致；仅有 2:1 比例不会自动判为全景。不支持双鱼眼、双目、VR180、裁切全景或厂商私有原片；普通与全景投影不能混合补拍。全景缓存不再设固定 20 GiB 上限，请预留足够磁盘空间；单幅解码仍限 512 MiB。格式、参数和验证范围见[全景视频](docs/PANORAMA_VIDEO_V1.md)、[全景图片](docs/PANORAMA_IMAGES_V1.md)与[补拍说明](docs/RESHOOT_V2.md)。

压缩 PLY、SPZ 和 SOG 不再按估算内存拒绝导出，但仍受实际内存、磁盘和格式约束影响；取消人为门槛不代表大模型一定能够导出。详见[导出说明与验证](docs/model-export-verification.md)。

### Gaussian 编辑快捷键

- 矩形选择时，左键拖动替换选区，`Shift + 左键拖动`添加，`Ctrl + 左键拖动`移除；中键旋转视角，右键平移，滚轮缩放。
- 黄色高亮表示当前选区；按 `Delete` 或 `Backspace` 删除选中 Gaussian，按 `Esc` 清空临时选区。
- 在矩形、球形或盒形选择中，点击“反选”或按 `Ctrl + I`（macOS 为 `⌘ + I`）切换保留或选中的部分。
- 球形或盒形选择会自动进入正交视图，可切换侧视图、正视图和顶视图，并通过视口控制器或数值面板调整位置与大小。
- 变换面板中的“场景操作轴”可切换“移动／旋转”，再次点击当前选中的按钮即可关闭；左键拖轴操作模型，拖动空白处转动视角。旋转环和面板旋转都围绕模型中心；松开提交一次编辑，`Esc` 取消本次拖轴，操作轴模式保存在本机。
- 使用 `WASD` 沿水平面漫游，`Shift` 三倍加速；编辑完成后可直接继续漫游，右下角滑轨支持0.1×–5.0×调速并记住本机设置。速度随缩放调整，仅透视视图可用。
- `Ctrl + Z` 撤销，`Ctrl + Shift + Z` 或 `Ctrl + Y` 重做。模型变换、裁切和删除共享同一历史记录；相机移动和临时黄色选区不计入历史。

## 处理流程

```text
输入视频或图片序列
  │
  ├─ 视频：FFprobe 分析，FFmpeg 按档位目标 FPS 或手动比例及工作分辨率抽帧；透明视频同步生成 RGBA 画面与 Mask
  ├─ 图片：快速扫描文件头并按文件名自然排序，复制源素材后优先硬链接复用；按需生成 Alpha Mask
  ├─ COLMAP：自动选择 CPU 或 CUDA GPU 提取特征；视频顺序匹配，图片默认穷举匹配，超过100张可确认按序匹配；顺序匹配沿用档位闭环检测规则
  ├─ COLMAP：增量重建并验证注册率和三维点，按需桥接补帧；仅实际透明素材启用两视图三角化
  ├─ 全景：先保留整幅 ERP 做球面重建，仅将已注册画面转为六面训练图片
  ├─ Brush：使用可用 GPU 训练 Gaussian Splats；精细档按原始训练分辨率规划
  └─ 校验 PLY 后原子发布为 final.ply
```

COLMAP 生成至少一张注册图像和有效三维点后，普通生成任务会继续进入 Brush。注册率低于 80% 时会给出质量警告，不会仅因注册率低而终止；补拍还要求至少一张新增画面成功注册。

图片序列预检只读取 JPG/PNG 文件头，检查数量、尺寸和 Alpha 通道，不提前解码全部像素。“检测到 Alpha 通道”不等于已经找到透明区域，生成时才检查实际透明度并按需启用 Mask。项目仍保留一份源素材副本；项目内的画面优先通过硬链接复用，不支持时回退复制，素材导入和画面准备期间会持续显示进度与日志。

## 系统要求

- Windows 11，x64。

- 视频导出需要 WebView2 提供 WebCodecs AVC 编码能力；不支持时仍可在“动画”模式播放效果，但“导出视频”会显示不可用原因。

5. 选择“快速”“均衡”或“精细”档位。

使用提示：

- 拖动左右面板之间的分界线可以调整宽度；双击分界线恢复默认比例。
- 点击右下角百分比按钮可缩小、恢复或放大整个界面。
- 新任务草稿会在本机保存，重启后重新检查素材。运行中的任务参数不能修改，但可以切换并编辑其他草稿；不能同时启动第二个任务。
- 新任务可拖动排序。“自动执行下一个任务”默认关闭，开启后按顺序执行，不跳过未就绪任务；图片顺序确认会暂停启动，取消则关闭队列。

- 沿用原模型时，从未经编辑的生成 PLY 初始化，旧图、新图共同使用正常完整训练配方，不另行缩短步数或降低学习率。只有确认拍摄设置相同且单相机、工作图片尺寸及方向兼容时才复用原内参。它不是完整断点续训，也不保证只改变新增区域；派生项目不继承删除或裁切。已有任务仍按原快照执行。实测范围见[补拍说明](docs/RESHOOT_V2.md)。

## 质量档位

原自动优化的基础策略现为默认设置。快速／均衡保留工作分辨率限制，精细档使用原始训练分辨率；不放大低分辨率素材。图片保留全部有效输入，视频可在档位上方分级调整抽帧比例，并保留按源 FPS 换算的精确默认档。

新策略、自动重试规则与兼容说明见[默认生成策略](docs/GENERATION_POLICY.md)；历史配方和开发环境配置见[参数配置](docs/pipeline-optimization-config.zh-CN.md)。

视频和已确认按序排列的图片默认使用档位对应的离线闭环检测，不保证所有素材均能闭环。补拍独立匹配新旧画面，新增画面之间沿用窗口10和档位闭环规则。自动补帧不受自动重试开关影响。

手动抽帧的新任务在初始注册率低于80%、存在有效初始模型时，可按未注册区间尝试一轮桥接补帧，最多额外补首次实际帧数的20%，且不超过源视频可用帧数。例如首次360张，最多再补72张；100%抽帧不再新增。首次帧数仍遵守最少30帧规则，源帧不足时全部采用。默认抽帧仍用下表的桥接候选预算。旧任务中断续跑保留原规则；1.2倍只是帧数预算，不保证耗时或成功率。详见[补帧规则与验证](docs/MANUAL_BRIDGE_V3.md)。

下表为普通素材。普通精细档按已注册训练图片的有效像素与平均重建轨迹长度计算 Splat 上限，系数为0.5；完全透明像素不计入，初始化点数不被削减。公式与适用范围见[精细档预算](docs/FINE_SPLAT_BUDGET.md)。

全景使用独立训练配方和点数预算。精细档保留原始 ERP，训练六面边长为 `floor(ERP宽度 / 4)`，不放大素材。点数预算按原始球面模型统计，不因六面转换乘六。所有上限均不保证实际点数、画质或显存安全。

| 档位 | 默认初始 / 桥接候选目标 | 视频工作长边 | COLMAP 长边 / 最大特征数 | Brush 训练 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 快速 | 6 / 9 FPS | 最大 1,600 | 1,200 / 4,096 | 8,000 iterations，最大分辨率 1,600 |
| 均衡 | 8 / 12 FPS | 最大 1,920 | 1,600 / 8,192 | 15,000 iterations，最大分辨率 1,920 |
| 精细 | 12 / 15 FPS | 原始分辨率 | 3,200 / 16,384 | 30,000 iterations，原始训练分辨率，有效像素／轨迹预算（系数0.5） |

短视频会尽量保留至少 30 张画面；源帧不足时使用全部可用画面。因此实际初始和候选采样率可能高于表中的目标值，但不会超过源帧率或源素材帧数。

精细档训练分辨率不再按显存分档。开启“自动重试”后，三个档位在明确 GPU OOM 时均可最多重试一次，上限取失败进程最后可信点数的80%，不降低分辨率；没有可信计数、无法实际降低或低于初始化点数时直接报错。兼容后端回退及自动补帧不受此开关控制。

旧任务的中断续跑保留原快照；失败任务手动重试采用新策略并归档不兼容工作缓存。原素材、已发布模型和编辑结果保持不变。
